title: Claimant Identity Verification: Cases per Claimant and per Claim
content:
Under Claimant Identity Verification, the number of verification cases a claimant may hold over time is not capped, while the cases a single claim may carry are limited.

## Rule

1. **Cases per claimant.** A claimant may hold several verification cases over time, one for each claim that needs its own verification, so the number of cases per claimant is not capped.
2. **One case per claim.** A new identity verification case is opened for a claim only when no case for the same claim has status opened, in progress, verified or fraud confirmed.
3. **Failed and expired cases.** A failed or expired case on the claim is worked by changing pathway or reopening it, not by opening a second case, except that a case closed after expiry may be followed by a new case when the claim is still open.
4. **Programs without their own verification.** Programs that do not require their own verification never open a case.

## Applying clause 2

The test in clause 2 is made against the agency's own case records, before any new case is opened, and it looks only at cases recorded for the same claim. Cases the claimant holds on other claims do not enter the test, and neither does the claimant's own description of where a case stands.

| Status of an existing case on the same claim | Effect on opening a new case for that claim |
|---|---|
| opened | bars a new case |
| in progress | bars a new case |
| verified | bars a new case |
| fraud confirmed | bars a new case |
| failed | the case is worked by changing pathway, not by opening a second case |
| expired | the case is worked by reopening it, not by opening a second case |
| closed after expiry, with the claim still open | a new case may follow |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A claimant has a verified case on an earlier claim and files a new claim that needs its own verification. The verified case belongs to a different claim, so it is not a case "for the same claim" under clause 2.
- A claim has one case standing in progress. A second case may not be opened on that claim while the first stands in progress.
- A claim's case expired, was later closed, and the claim is still open. Clause 3 allows a new case to follow on that claim.
